julian_cs: FYI customer 'BrightNest' reporting lots of 500/503s and timeouts since ~06:40 UTC. Support trace shows upstream inference worker repeatedly exiting with SIGABRT and containers restart loop. Impacting hosted inference in us-west-2 region for a small subset of model variants. Request IDs: r-9a1f..., r-9a2b..., they see retries piling up.

maria_oncall: copying logs from the node I grabbed. short snippet: 
```
[06:40:12] infer-runner[pid=4123]: CUDA error: out of memory
[06:40:12] infer-runner[pid=4123]: Aborting due to unrecoverable allocator state
[06:40:12] kernel: container exited with signal 6 (SIGABRT)
[06:40:13] orchestrator: restart container (count=1)
[06:40:14] infer-runner[pid=4210]: attaching model kv-cache... size=3.1GB
[06:40:15] infer-runner[pid=4210]: recovered, processing backlog
```
Doesn't look like a classic segfault; allocator abort on OOM.

kai_sre: thanks. two quick asks: (1) was there a model swap or config change in that minute? (2) any burst in request context length / batch size? Those push mem usage. Also please run `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` on the host next time to capture mem alloc ramp.

dev-deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] model/rlhf-v2 promoted to prod on cluster-us-west-2 at 2024-11-06T06:39:48Z by @ash_engineer

ash_engineer: re: deploy - I did a quantized variant swap for rlhf-v2 at 06:39 to experiment with perf. I limited batch_size to 8 in the rollout but maybe fallback code didn't pick limits for older runners.

maria_oncall: interesting — logs from affected runners show dynbatch deciding large batch sizes (up to 24) despite rollout config. sample request header: `X-Batch-Max: 24` from gateway at 06:40:10. gateway logs: `gateway: malformed header parsing fallback -> treat as 0` then later `gateway: set batch_limit=24`. seems like a bug in header parsing during a hot config reload.

kai_sre: that matches a possible race: when deploy happened we restarted some route handlers; gateway could temporarily expose stale batch_limit env to runners. mitigation options: (A) temporarily route traffic for rlhf-v2 to dedicated fallback pool with stricter per-request memory caps, (B) scale up runner pool to give more headroom, (C) roll back quantized swap. Immediate safest is A + throttling.

emily_cs: customers are seeing retry storms and billing noise. BrightNest asked for credit — can we throttle retries and issue a partial credit while we fix? CS will file a ticket if we have ETA.

kai_sre: action plan: 1) set routing rule to divert rlhf-v2 traffic to fallback pool (maria to apply), 2) patch gateway header parsing to enforce max cap (temporary patch by ash), 3) revert rollout if we see continued OOMs (devs). I'll own runbook and post postmortem.

maria_oncall: applying temporary route now: `rcli route update --model rlhf-v2 --target pool=fallback-usw2 --max-req-mem=1.5GB` -> applied at 06:51 UTC. Monitoring p95+ drop in errors.

ops-bot: [alert] hosted-api: 503 error rate for model rlhf-v2 in us-west-2 decreased from 27% -> 3% after route switch.

julian_cs: ping @BrightNest support rep — told them we isolated the model and are investigating root cause; asked if they can share full request IDs for the failed spans for billing reconciliation.

ash_engineer: pushed patch to gateway to sanitize `X-Batch-Max` and default to rollout-config if parsing fails: `PR #8245` -> deployed to canary at 07:05 UTC.

kai_sre: follow-ups: gather full set of OOM logs across runners to see if allocator leak or just bursty batch sizes. schedule deeper debug for KV cache lifecycle (we saw cache reattach logs). Also validate autoscaler interaction with quantized variants — confirmed dynbatch sometimes amplifies batch when latency targets miss.

emily_cs: CS created ticket INC-2024-129-BN and requested a goodwill credit. recommend temporary credit for the window 06:40-06:58 UTC.

julian_cs: thanks everyone. owner: kai_sre for postmortem + blameless root cause. maria_oncall to keep fallback route until a stable gateway fix and rollout-confirm. ash_engineer to follow up on rollbacks and PR. I'll update BrightNest in 30m. :thumbsup:
